If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I need a box, that is on the upside open. The outer dimensions are 220 x 300 x 160mm. The wall thickness should be 8mm and the bottom thickness 12mm | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step by step

1. Establish the solid outer shell  
   • Call the block-function once, with subtraction = False (first volume).  
   • Dimensions (x_size, y_size, z_size) = (220 mm, 300 mm, 160 mm).  
   • Basepoint (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0).

2. Remove the inner volume to obtain an open-top cavity  
   • Call the block-function a second time, this time with subtraction = True.  
   • Wall thickness = 8 mm, bottom thickness = 12 mm ⇒
     – Inner length = 220 – 2·8 = 204 mm  
     – Inner width  = 300 – 2·8 = 284 mm  
     – Inner height = 160 – 12 = 148 mm  
   • To keep uniform side-wall thickness and a 12 mm bottom, shift the inner block’s basepoint by (8, 8, 12).  
   • Dimensions (x_size, y_size, z_size) = (204 mm, 284 mm, 148 mm).  
   • subtraction = True so the volume is cut away.

3. No other primitives are required; the geometry is complete.

When you ask for it, I will prepare the two block-function calls exactly as described (outer solid first, inner subtraction second) and then wait for your explicit permission to execute.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
